result.summary:
24 of 26 screens passed on MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B. All of them are narrow lexical skills: roman numerals, ordinal words, greek letters, weekdays and colours. Nothing I tried came close to a selective unit for the broad skills (math, code, multilingual, facts).

The model is a Qwen3.5 hybrid: GatedDeltaNet linear attention with 32 heads of 128 dims, plus full attention at L3/7/.../31 with 16 heads of 256 dims. Its MLPs are 12288 wide.

Two weight recipes produced every passing part:
- **Late layers (L20–28), output writers:** take attribution seeds in one layer and grow the cluster to 64–512 units by each unit's down_proj logit-lens z-score on the skill's tokens.
- **Early layers (L8–14), input detectors:** grow seeds by each unit's silu(gate)·up response to the skill's token embeddings, compared with random tokens.
- **Heads:** rank them by how much of the skill's token energy lies in their out_proj columns.

| Skill | MLP clusters (target drop) | Head groups |
|---|---|---|
| roman_numeral | L28 64 (.484), 128 (.467); L26 64 (.536), 256 (.571), 512 (.548); L8 64 detectors (.16) | — |
| ordinal_word | L23 64 (.352), 128 (.35), 256 (.358); L14 128 detectors (.156) | L28 [25,6,26,23] (.735); L28 6-head (.736) |
| greek_letter_successor | L22 64 (.219), 128 (.221); L20 128 (.194); detectors at L8 64 (.261), L9 64 (.232), L9 128 (.236), L12 64 (.287), L13 64 (.228), L13 128 (.236) | L28 [28,29,1,23] (.209) |
| weekday_successor | L21 64 (.199) | — |
| color_of_object | L26 64 (.238) | — |

Caveats:
- **The L28 ordinal head groups are effectively one head.** Head 25 alone drops ordinal by .723, and 3 of 5 random 6-head groups also dropped it by about .72. Expect them to transfer like a single head.
- **Some random baselines were noisy.** In the L9 128-unit greek screen, random parts ranged from −.151 to +.088. In the L9 64-unit screen, one random part dropped greek by .089.
- **Two passes are marginal.** The L8 roman (.16) and L14 ordinal (.156) clusters only just cleared the .15 threshold.
- **Two screens failed.** L27 greek (64 units) dropped .227 on the search split but failed held-out. A 64-unit L25 greek cluster (.158) was only ablated, not screened, because its control moved too much (−.076).

What didn't work:
- **Broad skills:** math, code and multilingual dropped at most about .06 from any sub-layer part, including 512-unit code-writer clusters at L30/L31. My en_fr_translation skill was just as robust.
- **Whole blocks:** single-layer blocks always hit facts and several other skills at once.
- **Writers without seeds:** clusters of pure writer units with no attribution seeds were inert for months, countries, code and colour at L28. Colour also failed outside L26: L23/L27 seed clusters dropped only .05–.09.
- **Months:** early month detector clusters at L12 and L9 stayed clean but plateaued at .11–.13, even at 256 units, so I never screened a month unit.
- **Shared sequence units:**
  - L19 heads [1,9,11,13] hit month, ordinal, greek and weekday together.
  - L24 unit 6064 and L16 unit 1951 drive both month and greek.
  - L18 clusters and the L8/L11 seeds leak between weekday, ordinal and greek. The L11 greek detector cluster reached .245 but still leaked .118 into weekday after I excluded the month and weekday detectors.
- **Facts heads aren't separable:** L23 heads 8–11 drop facts .278 but colour .151 too.
- **Other attention:** full-attention head groups at L23/L27/L31 leaked into other skills' controls, and the late L30/L31 heads act as generic few-shot copy heads. The last linear-attention head groups I tried by OV energy (L26 roman, L22 weekday, L25 colour) were inert or not selective.

I hit the 8-skill cap, so I couldn't add the arithmetic, capitals and antonym skills I had planned. I'm stopping with about 10 minutes left and 34 screens unused.

result.summary: MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B (hybrid: full attention at L3,7,...,31, GatedDeltaNet elsewhere). No new screen passed in this short run (1 screen: L14 roman 128-unit cluster, roman .138 vs random max .024, but under .15 and failed held-out). Findings: (1) Country-writer MLP clusters (country unembedding subspace minus 1.5x other categories) at L24/L26/L30, 256-512 units, were inert for country_of_city (≤.03) even though the logit lens is clean (China/Egypt/Japan units). This matches the lesson that writer clusters are not causal when the skill has a large margin. (2) Whole blocks L14 and L20-21 were not selective (facts .45, general_text .21). (3) Attribution plus weight-cosine seed growth found: L14 u3335 is a roman-numeral unit (attribution .051). Its 64/128/256 clusters cut roman .12-.14 with control ≤.03, well above random. That is close to passing, so the next step is to add more L14 roman seeds. L11 roman 128 gave .117 (control .015). (4) L16 hosts a shared ordered-sequence successor hub: 128-unit clusters seeded on colour/country attribution dropped greek .50/.23, month .20/.26 and ordinal .29/.24. It is not selective for any single skill, but it is a candidate 'sequence successor' unit for compiling. (5) en_fr L20 seeds (u3850) and code L18 seeds grown to 128 were inert (<.05). Infra note: py: handles are lowercased, so save /work files with lowercase names.
